locationPrompt.title: Allow access to your location
locationPrompt.body: Kliuye works out the bite index from the weather right where you fish. Pressure, wind and water temperature change within 20–30 km, so a forecast for the whole region often misses.
locationPrompt.reasonWeather: The forecast and the best bite window are for the waters near you, not for a point somewhere in the region.
locationPrompt.reasonWaters: The map opens where you are and can route you to the water.
locationPrompt.reasonSea: We check whether the sea is near, so sea fish are not offered where there are none.
locationPrompt.privacy: Only your approximate location, and only while the app is open. Coordinates rounded to about 1 km go to the Open-Meteo weather service, and OpenFreeMap provides the map. We have no servers or accounts of our own — details in the privacy policy.
locationPrompt.manual: Pick a water on the map

tips.title: Tips
tips.subtitle: Drawn from what the weather is doing right now

pressureFalling.title: Fish the edge of the drop-off
pressureFalling.body: On falling pressure predators leave the holes and sit at two to three metres. Work the lure along the ledge, not across the bottom of the pit.

pressureRising.title: Go deeper and slow down
pressureRising.body: Rising pressure pins fish to the bottom. Work the holes, use long pauses and a smaller lure.

pressureSteady.title: Steady barometer, steady tactics
pressureSteady.body: With the pressure flat fish hold their usual spots. Start with proven marks and resist swapping lures too early.

windRipple.title: Stand so the wind hits the bank
windRipple.body: The chop pushes food to the leeward bank — baitfish follow, and predators follow them. Mirror-flat water is worse right now.

windStrong.title: Get behind a headland
windStrong.body: In strong wind look for sheltered bays and leeward points. A heavier lure keeps contact with the bottom.

windCalm.title: Finer and quieter
windCalm.body: In dead calm fish see everything. Thinner fluorocarbon, a smaller lure, a longer cast — and no banging around the boat.

waterWarming.title: Speed the retrieve up
waterWarming.body: Fish are no longer sluggish: pause two or three seconds instead of five, shorten the jerk. Warm water suits a 3″ twister and a minnow.

waterCooling.title: Slow everything down
waterCooling.body: Cooling water slows the metabolism. Long pauses, a smaller lure, and fish the deepest stretches.

waterSteady.title: Keep the usual rhythm
waterSteady.body: Water temperature is stable, so fish are not relocating. Revisit the same marks at different hours.

waterUnknown.title: Read the air instead
waterUnknown.body: There is no water reading — estimate it from the recent average air temperature and do not trust the forecast too precisely.

cloudBroken.title: Go bright and noisy
cloudBroken.body: In murky light fish key on contrast and vibration. Acid colours and wide-action lures beat natural ones.

cloudOvercast.title: Predators have spread over the shallows
cloudOvercast.body: Under full cloud fish are not afraid of open water. Cover the shallows and the mouth of the bay.

cloudClear.title: Look for shade and depth
cloudClear.body: In bright sun fish sit under snags, in bank shade and deep. Fish early, late, or in the shadows.

moonNew.title: Do not miss the morning window
moonNew.body: On a new moon the strongest phase is the first two hours after sunrise. Be on the water early, not at eight.

moonFull.title: A full moon shifts the bite to the night
moonFull.body: On a full moon fish feed at night and are sluggish in the morning. Plan a late evening or a very early start.

precipitationDrizzle.title: Drizzle is no reason to go home
precipitationDrizzle.body: Light rain knocks down surface glare and adds oxygen. The bite dies before a thunderstorm, not under drizzle.

precipitationHeavy.title: Sit the downpour out
precipitationHeavy.body: Heavy rain clouds the water and kills the bite. Wait for it to ease and fish the first hours after.

precipitationDry.title: In dry weather, work the clock
precipitationDry.body: With no rain the bite holds at dawn and dusk. In the middle of the day pick shade and depth.

timeDawn.title: The morning window is open
timeDawn.body: The most active hour of the day has already started. Do not spend it rigging up.

timeDusk.title: The evening session has begun
timeDusk.body: The last two hours of light are the day's second window. Take your best mark right now.

timeDay.title: Fish spots, not water
timeDay.body: Between the windows fish hold still. Work cover — snags, ledges, bank shade — instead of searching wide.

airWaterWarmer.title: The shallows have warmed — fish are there
airWaterWarmer.body: Air warmer than water means shallow ground heats fastest. Start there.

airWaterColder.title: A cold snap drives fish deep
airWaterColder.body: Air colder than water cools the shallows first. Work the holes and the drop-offs.

about.title: About
about.disclaimer: The bite index is an estimate based on open weather data. It is not a guarantee of a catch.
about.sources: Weather data and place search: Open-Meteo. Map: OpenFreeMap, built from OpenStreetMap; the map around your points is saved on the device for offline use. Map relief: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen) on AWS. Whether a point is on water is checked against the same OpenFreeMap vector data. The moon phase is computed on the device with Meeus's algorithm. Fish pictures: engravings by Marcus Elieser Bloch (1782–1795), public domain.
about.rules: Rules, closed seasons and licence requirements vary by region. Check local regulations before you go.
about.privacy: No sign-up, no analytics, no ads. Your profile (name, photo, settings), journal and saved places stay on this phone only and are never sent anywhere. To get a forecast, coordinates rounded to about 1 km are sent to Open-Meteo; the map and water data come from OpenFreeMap, and place names from your phone's own geocoder. Crash reports only if you turn them on in Settings: anonymous, via Sentry, on servers in the EU. Details are in the privacy policy.

howItWorks.title: How the index works
howItWorks.linkLabel: How do we work it out?
howItWorks.linkHint: The factors, their weight, and what the index cannot know
howItWorks.intro: The 0–100 index shows how much the weather right now favours fish feeding. We take the Open-Meteo forecast for your point, rate each factor from "hurts" to "helps" and add them up with the weights below. Then the species and the season are taken into account.

factor.pressure: The biggest factor. Fish feed best on steady or slowly falling pressure; a sharp jump either way shuts the bite down.
factor.waterTemperature: The closer the water is to the species' comfort range, the higher the score. At sea we use marine data; in fresh water, an estimate from the last days' weather.
factor.wind: A light ripple beats both dead calm and a gale. Wind blowing onto your bank adds points: it pushes food there.
factor.moon: New and full moon bring the strongest feeding pushes; the quarters are neutral.
factor.timeOfDay: Peaks just after sunrise and before sunset. How strong they are differs by species.
factor.cloudCover: Broken cloud beats a clear sky, which keeps predators hiding in cover.
factor.precipitation: Drizzle helps, a downpour does not. Dry weather is neutral.
factor.airWaterDelta: Air slightly warmer than the water means a stable day. A cold snap over warm water drives fish deep.

howItWorks.species: Every species has its own profile: its comfortable water temperature, how much pressure changes put it off, how much wind it tolerates, and how strong its morning and evening peaks are. That is why on the same day pike can score 80 and bream 45.
howItWorks.season: Finally the score is multiplied by the species' seasonal factor, taken from angling calendars. During spawning or out of season the index drops, and sea fish are not scored at all far from the sea. Sea fish are also scored only where they live: there is no cod in the Black Sea and no horse mackerel off Norway. The same goes for fresh water: no wels catfish in Africa, and no carp high in the mountains, where trout live. And no trout in a warm lowland such as the Donbas steppe.
howItWorks.limits: Depth, the shape of the bottom, current, water clarity, other anglers, and whether the fish actually live in this water. It is an estimate from open weather data, not a promise of a catch.
howItWorks.presenceTitle: The per-species index is not a fish map
howItWorks.presence: The index shows how active a species is in the current weather, not whether that fish lives in this water. If there are no pike here, a high pike index will not put them there.
howItWorks.speciesNote: The index shows how active a species is in the current weather, not whether that fish lives in this water. Check local fishing rules.

index.title: Where the index comes from

explainer.title: Where does this number come from?
explainer.body: It is not a weather forecast and not a random figure. The 0–100 index is built from 8 weather factors, each with its own weight. These matter most:
explainer.more: We also count the moon phase, time of day, rain and cloud, then the species and the season. The index shows how active fish are in this weather, not that they are sure to be in this water.
